title: Answer what the host starts, the way its specification says

blocks.text: A new acquirer link, `acq-mux`, goes live next week, and the host's certification team ran their network management script against it today. Their report:

items: echoes, sign-ons, sign-offs, key changes and the nightly cutover advice all went unanswered;
the client is required to stop sending purchases when the host signs the link off, and to sign on again once the host accepts sign-ons;
the host must never receive a key back from a client, and must not be told a key is in place when it isn't;
a function the client does not know must not be approved.

blocks.text: Write the listener that answers them: `NetworkRequests` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/NetworkRequests.java`. The host's rules for these messages are copied into its class comment. They are not the same as the page's. Finish `process` and `resultFor`, the two methods marked `TODO`. About twenty lines in total. The `KeyInstaller` you are given does the security module's part.
The tests put the host's messages on the in queue of a real QMUX that has your listener, and read what comes out on its out queue.

cases.says: the host's 0800 echo is answered on the link with an 0810 carrying its fields 7, 11 and 70 and 39=00
the host's own sign-on is answered 00 and changes no mark
a host's 0100, a late 0210 and an 0810 are not answered and go on to the unhandled queue
a host sign-off removes both the enabled and the logon mark, so the pool stops and the manager signs on again
the answer is built from the fields an 0810 carries, so the key in field 48 is not sent back
a key change is acknowledged only when the installer put the key in place; otherwise it is refused with 06
an 0820 advice and its repeat 0821 are acknowledged with an 0830 and 39=00
an 0800 whose function the client does not know is refused, not approved

origin.section: 15.5 A New Key Is Acknowledged Only Once It Is Installed

concepts: Each host-initiated network management request is answered by its function, from a list of fields, through its source: a sign-off removes the enabled and logon marks, an unknown function is refused, advices are acknowledged with 0830, and other messages are left to the next listener.
A key change is answered 00 only after the key is imported, its check value matches and it is stored; otherwise it is refused, the old key stays, and the key never travels back in the answer.
